why_points: The pick: Receptions higher 2.5 on PrizePicks. Each pick has to win 57% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line) is 62%.
Game log, most recent first: 3, 3, 2, 6, 7, 2. Weighted average 3.6; went higher than 2.5 in 4 of 6 games (74% recency-weighted).
Trending down: last 3 games average 2.7 vs 5.0 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±1.7, so the line is 0.6 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a meaningful gap.
Matchup: Buffalo is about league-average against WRs.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): +15% on his average.
PFF: Buffalo plays man on 18% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 27%); he gains 1.57 yds/route vs man and 2.09 vs zone → +2% from scheme.

Projection: we expect 3.6 catches on average; in a typical game 3.1 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.6 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 68% and the matchup 68%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights borrowed from NFL week 2 - college has no calibration yet), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 63%, matchup 63%.
Bottom line: we give it 63% to win and it needs 57%. The edge is the difference: +6.1 points; that works out to about +11¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
